Title: May 21, 2026 - Boulder City Council Regular Meeting (open comment, consent agenda, call-up check-ins, public hearing on Adjustment to Base Budget One, and matters from mayor and council on study sessions and straw polls)
Overview: Council heard extensive open comment on San Lazaro mobile home park residents seeking to buy their park, airport local control, Golden West senior housing utility changes, and minimum wage. It approved the consent agenda 8-0 except for Wallach's no vote on item 3B, and unanimously adopted Ordinance 8750 (Adjustment to Base Budget One, about $18.6 million). Council then discussed clarifying study session practice, straw poll terminology, and reconsideration rules, agreeing to use 'non-binding nod of five' language and to document informational study sessions in the rules of procedure.

Topic1.Title: Open comment: San Lazaro mobile home park purchase
Topic1.Summary: Multiple residents of San Lazaro mobile home park spoke about a notice of sale and risk of displacement, asking the city to help residents buy the park. A steering committee described a $42.5 million purchase price and concerns about private equity ownership. Staff said the city and county agreed to a new appraisal, that financial support options are being explored, and that the city supports the effort.

Topic2.Title: Open comment: airport local control and ballot measure
Topic2.Summary: Several speakers urged council to maintain local control of the municipal airport and avoid FAA grant obligations, citing noise, leaded fuel, and aviation safety. Others argued the airport is a science and disaster-response resource. Speakers asked for a ballot measure and a do-over on study session information. Staff responded that funding decisions and CDOT funding limits are under review and the airport will return to council soon.

Topic3.Title: Open comment: Golden West senior housing utilities and parking
Topic3.Summary: Golden West residents, many seniors on fixed incomes, said the Boulder Housing Partners lease change ending bundled cable, TV and telephone service would cost them, and raised parking fees and elevator problems. Staff said the Comcast contract expired, free Wi-Fi continues, and rents drop about $40 to $45 per month, but additional services cost more. Council asked BHP for follow-up information and support options.

Topic4.Title: Open comment: minimum wage and vacancy tax
Topic4.Summary: A resident opposed a proposed refusal to raise the tipped minimum wage in line with a 2024 study, arguing that wage freezes reduce buying power and drive workers away. He proposed a Boulder vacancy tax to address rising rents instead. Another speaker asked the city to speed up development review for trees and energy-efficient homes. Council received these comments as part of open comment.

Topic5.Title: Consent agenda approval (items 3A and 3B)
Topic5.Summary: Council approved the consent agenda, which included items 3A and 3B, by voice roll call. Councilmember Wallach voted no on item 3B, an ordinance amending Title 7 height limitations, citing sloppy drafting. The motion passed with that one exception.

Topic6.Title: Call-up check-ins: 777 Broadway site review and 990 Arapahoe landmark
Topic6.Summary: Council reviewed call-up items for a site review at 777 Broadway for 63 residential units and a Landmarks Board decision not to designate 990 Arapahoe Avenue. No one called up either item. Councilmember Matt then commented on the landmarking process, suggesting reform at next year's retreat because of its effect on senior affordable housing and displacement.

Topic7.Title: Public hearing: Ordinance 8750, Adjustment to Base Budget One
Topic7.Summary: Staff presented the first 2026 adjustment to base totaling about $18.6 million, including $13.1 million from fund balance, $5.3 million from mid-year grants, and $129,000 from additional revenue. Items included business incentives, wildfire programs, affordable housing carryover, and a $7.3 million radio replacement purchased early at a discount. Council questioned fund balance levels and communications staffing, and the ordinance was adopted unanimously after a public hearing with no speakers in favor or against.

Topic8.Title: Matters from mayor and council: study sessions, straw polls, and reconsideration
Topic8.Summary: City Attorney Teresa Tate explained that study sessions give non-binding direction to staff, that straw polls are not addressed in procedure, and that reconsideration applies only after a material change in law or fact, requiring five votes to schedule. Council discussed the confusion from a recent study session on the airport and agreed to use 'non-binding nod of five' language. Council also agreed to document informational study sessions in the rules of procedure and to review CAC agenda item titles.
